physicalNotes: Radius: MASCARA-1 is a rapid rotator. Hooton et al. (2022), A&A 658, A75 fit the CHEOPS and Spitzer transits of MASCARA-1 b with a gravity-darkened oblate star: equatorial radius 2.082 solar radii and a polar radius 4.39% smaller (Table 5), so a polar radius of 1.9906. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, (2.082^2 x 1.9906)^(1/3) = 2.0511 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202141645); the scene draws the flattening, with the equatorial radius on the outline. Mass 1.9 +/- 0.063 solar masses from Hooton et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of MASCARA-1 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 7490 +/- 150 K from Hooton et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of MASCARA-1 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis, the spin axis measured against MASCARA-1 b's orbit, is up.
